title: Quantitative Comparisons

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: Column A: $7\times8$. Column B: $6\times9+2$. Compare the two columns: which is greater, are they equal, or is it impossible to determine?
Column A: $123+456$. Column B: $700-120$. Compare the two columns.
Column A: $25\%$ of $160$. Column B: $20\%$ of $200$. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the result of increasing $100$ by $10\%$ twice in a row. Column B: the result of increasing $100$ by $20\%$ once. Compare the two columns.
Given $x=5$. Column A: $2x+3$. Column B: $x+8$. Compare the two columns.
questions.target: Algebraic comparisons at a fixed value

questions.q: For any real number $x$: Column A: $x$. Column B: $x^2$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $x=2$: $B>A$. If $x=\frac{1}{2}$: $A>B$. If $x=1$: $A=B$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.
questions.explanation: If $x=2$: $B>A$. If $x=\frac{1}{2}$: $A>B$. If $x=1$: $A=B$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.

questions.q: Given only that $n$ is an integer: Column A: $n^2$. Column B: $4$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $n=1$: $A=1<4$. If $n=3$: $A=9>4$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.
questions.explanation: If $n=1$: $A=1<4$. If $n=3$: $A=9>4$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.

sections.heading: Part II — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Intermediate Multi-Step Application (8–14)

questions.q: Column A: the perimeter of a square with side $6$ cm. Column B: the perimeter of a rectangle with length $8$ cm and width $3$ cm. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the area of a circle with radius $4$ cm (use $\pi\approx3.14$). Column B: the area of a square with side $7$ cm. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon. Column B: the sum of the interior angles of two triangles. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs $5$ and $12$. Column B: $14$. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the value of $x$, if $x:12=3:4$. Column B: $10$. Compare the two columns.
A recipe uses flour and sugar in the ratio $3:1$. Column A: the sugar needed for $240$ g of flour. Column B: $90$ g. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the sum of the parts in the simplified form of the ratio $18:24$. Column B: $8$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: $18:24$ simplifies to $3:4$, so the sum of parts is $3+4=7$. $B=8$. $B>A$.
questions.explanation: $18:24$ simplifies to $3:4$, so the sum of parts is $3+4=7$. $B=8$. $B>A$.

sections.heading: Part III — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: Two numbers are in the ratio $5:3$, and their sum is $96$. Column A: the larger number. Column B: $61$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: Total parts $=5+3=8$, each part $=12$. Larger number $=5\times12=60$. $B=61$. $B>A$.
questions.explanation: Total parts $=5+3=8$, each part $=12$. Larger number $=5\times12=60$. $B=61$. $B>A$.

questions.q: A data set is $4,7,7,9,13$. Column A: the mean. Column B: the median. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the range of the data set $3,8,15,22$. Column B: $20$. Compare the two columns.
A bag contains 3 red balls and 5 blue balls. Column A: the probability of drawing a red ball. Column B: the probability of drawing a blue ball. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the total cost of 4 items at 15 riyals each, after a $10\%$ discount on the total. Column B: $55$ riyals. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: Total before discount $=4\times15=60$ riyals. After discount: $60\times0.9=54$ riyals. $B=55$. $B>A$.
questions.explanation: Total before discount $=4\times15=60$ riyals. After discount: $60\times0.9=54$ riyals. $B=55$. $B>A$.

questions.q: Ali's age is $3$ years more than twice Sara's age. Sara is $8$. Column A: Ali's age. Column B: $20$. Compare the two columns.
